Try not to get Kaiden killed simulator.

[b]PROS:[/b]
+ great sci-fi setting
+ amazing story arcs
+ cool soundtrack
+ exploring the choices made in previous games
+ another awesome cast of characters
+ fun multiplayer
+ (after some time all DLCs have been added by default to the base game)

[b]CONS:[/b]
- Origin
- infamous ending
- Steam version is RIDICULOUSLY buggy
- [strike]cut-out DLC characters[/strike] (now included in the base game)

[b]Special review section for EA games:[/b]
[u]Should you play?[/u] YEAH
[u]Should you BUY???[/u] NOT ON STEAM

[b]Comment:[/b]
A lot of criticism has been made about this game when it came out and many of it was correct. I played it back then (hence the low play time here) but getting to it back now made me think more about it. And I dare say the ending doesn't wrap up the decisions of the trilogy but the whole game itself takes them and nicely drives them home.

There were many emotional scenes and tough decisions in ME3 and apart from the lackluster ending the story telling is great. Many characters get a beautiful conclusion to their journeys, whether happy or tragic is up to you. Only the added Cerberus villain plot could have been withheld. Maybe expand it a little bit, but too much time was spent on it. Especially when we have the ultimate enemy - Reapers - to explore. This is also why the ending is so criticized, it focuses on the wrong stuff that not even the extended cut DLC could salvage.

Gameplay is just slightly tweaked ME2, so pretty good overall. Speaking of - multiplayer takes it and actually expands it by letting you play as other races too which I wish another ME game would finally touch upon. It's ridden with microtransactions though so there's that.

If you played the first two you HAVE TO finish the trilogy. I enjoyed my time with it when it came out, for the most part.

Now to address the version we have here on Steam. Doesn't count time played. When it launches in Origin it makes Steam stop recording the game is played. Had to bolster play time with Configuration Utility to be able to make a review. And the Configuration Utility doesn't detect settings properly. There are workarounds but it's bizarre considering I had to use none in the Origin version. Best part is that they won't bother to fix any issues since Legendary Edition is out now. Why even sell it on Steam if it's in such a bad shape here...?

[b]*Note:[/b] There is [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1328670/Mass_Effect_Legendary_Edition/]Mass Effect Legendary Edition[/url] available. It contains all games from the trilogy and most of their DLC. Honestly, Origin-only ME3 is cool but the Steam version is hot garbage. Just play it in the Legendary Edition, having all three games in one package is a nice bonus. Although you do lose out on multiplayer there...
------------------------------------------------------------------
[b]If you liked this review you can find more on the [/b][url=http://store.steampowered.com/curator/28638055-Subjective-Reviews-Corner/][u]Curator page[/u][/url][b] or in my [/b][url=http://steamcommunity.com/groups/srcorner][u]Review Corner[/u][/url][b].[/b]

At long last, we finally arrive at the end of a long journey. For those of you who were not a part of the EA divorce from Valve, you have no idea how long a wait it was to complete this game. After Mass Effect 2, EA games no longer were on steam and we were forced to either use a buggy defective system or not play. However, now they are back on Steam, albeit requiring the horrible Origin secondary logon. 

So what can I say about the last game in a trilogy. Well, I will get the most controversial part out of the way. As this is the digital deluxe edition, the endings have been redone a bit to be longer and more substantial. However, they still take away from the main aspect of the game “Choices have consequences”. To an extent, there are multiple endings. However there are 4 core endings and your results from the 3 games and doing the included multiplayer will determine what is included in 3 of the endings.

Each game changes up several of the mechanics of the game and this one is no different. The planet scanning is streamlines with less interaction. However you do have to worry about Reapers attacking if you do to much scanning. Combat has been tweaked again, and various other items.

Then we have the biggest change. Your objective this time around is to collect an army to go back to earth and fight the reapers. This introduces the EMS system or Effective Military Strength. Basically everything you do increases the number and you need to get to a certain percentage to upgrade your 3 core endings. 

This is where the multiplayer game comes in. From what I hear, multiplayer was removed from legendary edition so the numbers have been updated. Your readiness score has a 50% starting point that does not raise unless you do multiplayer. So if you have an 80% EMS, your results are actually 40%. I am not a fan of multiplayer shooters, however this was not bad. The loot system was horrible as it uses a card system purchased using in game currency from doing missions over and over. A successful mission is 11 rounds and making it out.

A final set of notes. The graphics now are quite dated. The community has created some impressive mods to rectify that to include re-adding controller support to the game. So if you want the updated experience, know it is available but requires a bit of work.

At the end of the day, if you have played the previous 2, you are either going to get this as it is cheaper or buy the legendary edition for the updated tweaks and free mods they stole and incorporated.

The game is awesome! Stop thinking about things and save the universe again Sheppard… If not, we will have to deal with that other commander from Andromeda 

We all know Origin is a horrible system and is the cause for soooooooo many issues that each player is talking about. I literally spent 2 weeks trying to get my game working again due to EA. The fact of the matter is that we are stuck with the system. If we want to play the final chapter…   :-(
